question: Who led the Indian National Congress at its first annual session?
solution:
The correct answer is __**WC Banerjee.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian National Congress:-**

 
 
• The first annual session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay (now Mumbai) on December 28, 1885.
 
• **The session was presided over by Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee, a prominent Indian barrister and political leader. **
 
 
 
• **WC Banerjee:-**
 
 
• **Bonnerjee was a key figure in the early Indian nationalist movement and played a pivotal role in establishing the Indian National Congress. **
 
• He was a moderate nationalist who believed in working within the British system to achieve Indian self-rule.
 
• He was also a strong advocate for social reform and education.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Surendranath Banerjee:-**

 
 
• **He was a Bengali barrister, journalist, and politician. **
 
• He was the founder of the Indian National Association, one of the first political organizations in India.
 
• Banerjee was a strong advocate for Indian self-rule and a vocal critic of British rule.
 
• He was also a leading figure in the Indian independence movement and served as the president of the Indian National Congress three times.
 
 
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji:-**
 
 
• **He was a Parsi barrister, economist, and politician. **
 
• He was known as the "Grand Old Man of India" for his long and distinguished career in public service.
 
• Naoroji was a leading advocate for Indian self-rule and a strong critic of British economic exploitation of India.
 
• He was also a pioneer in the field of Indian economics and is credited with developing the "drain of wealth" theory, which argued that British rule was draining India of its wealth. Naoroji served as the president of the Indian National Congress twice.
 
 
 
• **Allan Octavian Hume:-**
 
 
• **He was a British civil servant who played a key role in the founding of the Indian National Congress. **
 
• Hume was concerned about the growing discontent among Indians under British rule and believed that a political organization could help to channel that discontent in a constructive way.
 
• He invited a group of Indian leaders to meet in Bombay in 1885 to discuss the formation of such an organization.
 
• The meeting was a success, and the Indian National Congress was born.
 
• Hume served as the first general secretary of the Indian National Congress.
